title: Ribbon runs: Positive proof strip
summary: A run is a maximal consecutive group of identical characters. Produce its length for each run, from left to right. Spaces are characters too. Return only the strictly positive values in the derived sequence, preserving their relative order and duplicates.
descriptionMd:
A sticking key leaves repeated marks across a typewriter ribbon's inspection strip. Ada prepares a clean proof strip for the front desk. Positive derived readings keep their places relative to one another.

A run is a maximal consecutive group of identical characters. Produce its length for each run, from left to right. Spaces are characters too.

Return only the strictly positive values in the derived sequence, preserving their relative order and duplicates.

Implement ribbonRunsPositiveProofStrip(line, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.

The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys (earlier units are used while the first two levels establish the foundations).
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
The line contains ASCII characters; the only word separator is a space.

Target time O(n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.

referenceSolutions.python:
def ribbonRunsPositiveProofStrip(line, k):
    a=line
    out=[]
    i=0
    while i<len(a):
        j=i+1
        while j<len(a) and a[j]==a[i]: j+=1
        out.append(j-i)
        i=j
    return [x for x in out if x>0]
